title: half-life: opposing force
text: We all know Half-Life is the classic. If you enjoyed Half-Life... you may find Opposing Force a little disappointing. In brief; Opposing Force puts you in the shoes of Adrian Shepard... one of the Soldiers sent in to 'clean up' Black Mesa.  Of course things go horribly wrong and you wind up fighting for your survuival and the fate of the world. The Good: * Most of the good things about Half-Life carry over. * New and interesting Enemies * New and interesting Weapons to kill New and Interesting Enemies with. * Explore New Areas of Black Mesa All in all a solid expansion and the idea of having a squad of specialize d soldiers to help you with is always great and leads to some interesting challenges. The Alien X Race also makes for tough antagonists. THe new black ops are also a joy. The Bad * Mundane Area Design. * Bad Lighting * Disjointed STory * Gimmicky Yeah, the biggest problem here is the lighting. I know Gearbox thought their Light Amp thingie was cool and it admittedly better than the flash light but... it's not practically to have the areas so dark you have to leave it on half the txchuffin time. You will be seeing alot of green in this game. Also the level design ... is dodgey. As in you don't quite feel the interconnection between the areas. In short they feel more like levels and less like actual parts pof a facility in some cases. A minor quibble. Also there are a timed few trial and error sections that will annoy you. Lastly it does feel Gimmickjy. SInce you spend most of your time fighting the allien X creatures... it's actually easy to forget that you're in the same Black Mesa as Gordon freeman and Barney Calhoun. It Might as well have been a different facility all together. Out of the two expansions this feels like the most tangental of them, and the least polished. There's also not much of the story being woven into the background, and it simply lacks the pacing of either Half-Life or Blue Shift. Not that it is a bad game.. it's still quite good but it is a step down rather than hup. Thankffully Half Life raised the bar enough that even a step down is still a high mark.

title: half-life: opposing force
text: After finishing "Half-Life," I decided to go and see what was done to improve upon the original game. I first started with this game, "Half-Life: Opposing Force." And when I played it, this game was a testament to how Expansion Packs were in their day, before the age of DLC. It expands upon the original game, with a good story and plenty of new stuff to make it feel like it's own game. This is what I remember fondly about expansion packs from back in the 1990s-2000s. Maintaining what made the original "Half-Life" work in the first place, "Half-Life: Opposing Force" is a concurrent story that takes place at the same time as the main game itself. This time, you play as Marine Corporal Adrian Shephard, who is part of the Marine Hazardous Environment Combat Unit (HECU) as they move to "cleanse" the Black Mesa facility during the events of the original "Half-Life." This game does a great job bridging together moments between this game and the original, making it feel like it's taking place during the main story. Again, Shephard is not a speaking protagonist, making him more immersive to the player. And again, you never lose control of Shephard throughout the game, therefore making it be told completely through his perspective.  What worked very well in the first game works very well in this Expansion. Also, the game continues to keep the game's areas interconnected, allowing you to feel like you're travelling through the Black Mesa facility. It again, worked in the first game, and works well in this one. I also liked the new weapons in this game, a Desert Eagle, a Sniper Rifle, a SAW, some new alien weapons, and even one of those Barnacles. There's plenty of new content and new areas to explore in this game that keep it fresh. I honestly found myself enjoying this game more than I did the original "Half-Life", and it felt like it corrected several of the flaws the original had. For one, the game doesn't give you as hard a time trying to maintain the power levels of the PCV. Also, the game avoids death-trap level design as much as the original did. There's still plenty of platforming with bad jump controls, but overall, I didn't have as many problems with this game as I did the original. I still like the original, but I feel this game felt more perfected. I also liked how this game gave you more useful allies (security guards and scientists aren't much help except for opening doors), but the other Marines in this game are a little more useful (especially the Engineer and Medic), but I found myself preferring to work alone, as the AI for the other Marines makes them not at all that useful in combat. Also, the enemy variety is improved quite a bit in this game, especially the Race X aliens, which also add on to the variety. This is another thing that makes this game a true testament to the expansion pack. It's a shame that most DLC doesn't have the quality that most old-time Expansion Packs did, but this game is a testament to the expansion pack of the 1990s-2000s. It has plenty of new content, enough of a story, plenty of new enemies, and improves on the original game's flaws. This is a great expansion that I enjoyed greatly. I look forward to another playthrough.

title: halo: spartan assault
text: It maintains all the core elements of Halo. The art style is similar, enemies act as they do in the mainstream games. It even brings back some of the forgotten elements from previous games, such as the wolverine and grizzly from Halo Wars, or the SMGs that haven't been seen since Halo 3. The levels are also small enough to play if your short on time, while at the same time each is unique and interesting. The story and music aren't to the quality of previous games though. It is to be expected for the budget of what was previously an iOS game but regardless, is lacking. It is also missing the Co-op mode included with other versions, and we've been given no explanation for its removal. All in all though, if you like the Halo series and are open to new things or just want an inexpensive top down shooter with solid gameplay, I suggest trying this game.

title: hero academy
text: I love this game, Its not really a game you sit down and play, Its more of a game you leave running in the background while you work / do other things, as you only really play for 10 seconds every few hours, unless you get an opponent on at around the same time as you. Its quite like a weird game of chess, except you place your pieces on the board and have 5 moves, each per turn. With 6 playable races, and 6+ pieces per race it has a huge mix of pieces. The "king" (crystal) is a 1 or 2 unmoving pieces on the board with a large amount of health, but most players protect their crystals and games are won and lost when a player looses all 20 of there pieces. Each faction also has a healer, that can bring pieces back, so there are additional tactical elements, "stomping" downed pieces, and protecting healers with higher heath or less valuable (pawns) units. While there are some training missions Its all Player Vs Player, and as such you get a mix of Skilled and Unskilled I run about 10+ games so I always have some moves to play when I open up the game. Some players Make there move instantly (takes about 30 seconds to update) some play a move every few hours/days You can replay players and setup multiple games with players This game is also an APP on Mobile devices, and you can share your account across them.

title: hero siege
text: This is a great game to remember the time spent as youth in front of our parent's computer playing Diablo 2.  After probably more than 100 offline hours into the game, there are a few bothersome points that stick out.  But to be very clear - I enjoyed myself for a great many hours with this baby, and its great and easy to pick back up and slay some demons. There really is no story here.  No true cutscenes, other than main character constantly standing over the dead body of fallen bosses, and nothing to tug on the heart strings.  Why are we slaying demons?  As silly as that sounds, after 100 hours, I don't know anymore.  Play too long in one sitting and you might start feeling bad for the constantly spawning masses whose life expectancy is little more than 30 seconds.  Surely hell or inferno or whatever place these buddies crawl out from is running low... Avoid potions in critcal situations and hardcore mode.  Maybe my guys had brain damage, but without regard to the spinning masses of chaos, blood and magic swirling all around, they enjoyed raising a new potion over their head and holding a pose for a second or two, while evil continued its assault unabated. Finally, get ready to grind and rush.  Although, if you remember Diablo 2 with any intellectual honesty, thats nothing new here.  I really took a liking to the cathedral, act 6 part 2, since it is largely devoid of traps.  Traps are the big killer in this game, an arrow to the head or some punji sticks underneath will end your adventure faster than any mortar chucking gargantuan abomination. I really like this game, but to be clear, I enjoy it for its mindless play, not for deep emotional inspiration.
